pages.title:
Built for how Africa
actually moves money.
pages.lede: A decade of work made money move across the continent. What sits on top of those rails is still a ledger with a search box. gabis is the layer that reads them and acts.

sections.heading: Why we exist
sections.body: A Lagos merchant’s money moves across a bank account, mobile money, cash, informal credit and two currencies. Every transaction is recorded somewhere. Almost none of it is ever turned into a decision. We are building the software that closes that gap — not another app that waits to be told what to do.

sections.heading: What we have shipped
sections.body: A working multi-currency product: accounts, cards, transfers, FX, invoicing with instalment schedules, bill payments, an AI copilot that reasons over your own transactions, and a collections agent that places real calls. Founder-built, running code, not mockups.

sections.heading: How we think about your money
sections.body: The deterministic core computes your financial state on device — categorisation, commitments, burn rate, what is genuinely spare. Numbers that cannot hallucinate. A model only ever phrases and explains them, and nothing moves without your explicit approval.

sections.heading: Where we are going
sections.body: Every African business will have a financial brain. gabis starts as the copilot that reads your money and the agent that collects it, and ends as the intelligence layer merchants, freelancers and institutions run their financial lives on.

pages.lede: The agreement between you and gabis when you use our apps and services. Written to be read, not to be survived.

sections.heading: Who we are
sections.body: gabis is a financial technology company, not a bank. Money remittance and banking services are provided by our licensed financial institution partners. Where those partners impose their own terms on an account or card, those terms apply alongside these.

sections.heading: Your account
sections.body: You must give accurate information when you open an account and keep it current. You are responsible for your credentials and for activity carried out with them. We may ask you to verify your identity before raising limits, and we may limit or suspend an account where we are required to, or where we reasonably suspect fraud.

sections.heading: Using the services
sections.body: You agree not to use gabis for anything unlawful, for payments you are not entitled to make, or in a way that puts our partners or other users at risk. We may refuse or reverse a transaction where we are legally required to do so, or where completing it would breach these terms.

sections.heading: Fees and rates
sections.body: Fees are shown before you confirm a transaction. Conversion uses the mid-market rate at the moment you confirm, with the fee stated as a separate line rather than folded into the rate. We will tell you before any fee changes take effect.

sections.heading: Automation and approvals
sections.body: Features that act on your behalf — payment reminders, collections calls, payday sweeps — only run within limits you set and only after you approve them. Nothing moves money without an explicit confirmation from you.

sections.heading: Liability
sections.body: We take responsibility for our own failures and for money we hold incorrectly. We are not liable for losses caused by inaccurate details you supply, by your own device or credentials being compromised, or by events outside our reasonable control.

sections.heading: Closing your account
sections.body: You can close your account at any time once your balance is settled. We will give you notice before closing an account ourselves, except where the law requires otherwise.

sections.heading: Changes and contact
sections.body: We may update these terms; material changes are notified in the app before they take effect. Questions go to legal@gabispay.com.

pages.title: Privacy policy.
pages.lede: What we collect, why we hold it, and what we will never do with it. Your transaction history is the most personal thing you will give us and we treat it that way.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.body: Identity and contact details you give us when opening an account; verification documents where regulation requires them; transaction records created by your use of the service; and device and usage data needed to keep accounts secure.

sections.heading: Why we hold it
sections.body: To operate your account, to meet anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer obligations, to prevent fraud, and to provide the features you asked for. We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with advertisers.

sections.heading: On-device reasoning
sections.body: The copilot computes your financial state on your device wherever it can — categorisation, recurring commitments, burn rate, affordability. That analysis does not require sending your full transaction history anywhere. Where a request needs a model, only the specific context for that question is sent, and never for advertising.

sections.heading: Who we share with
sections.body: Our licensed financial institution partners, so payments can actually settle; identity verification providers; and authorities where we are legally compelled. Each receives the minimum needed to do their part.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.body: For as long as your account is open, and afterwards for the period financial regulation requires us to retain records. After that it is deleted.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can ask for a copy of your data, ask us to correct it, or ask for deletion where no legal retention duty applies. Write to privacy@gabispay.com and we will respond within 30 days.

pages.ctaBody: privacy@gabispay.com — access, correction or deletion requests.

pages.title: Security.
pages.lede: How your money and your data are protected, and what we ask of you. Written plainly, because security advice nobody reads protects nobody.

features.title: Encryption everywhere
features.body: Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Credentials are never stored in plain text.

features.title: Device-level access
features.body: Biometric unlock and device binding, so a stolen password alone is not enough.

features.title: Approval before money moves
features.body: Every money-moving action is confirmed by you. No automation bypasses that.

features.title: Fraud monitoring
features.body: Unusual activity is flagged and, where necessary, held until you confirm it was you.

sections.heading: What we will never ask for
sections.body: We will never ask for your PIN, your password, or a one-time code — not by phone, not on WhatsApp, not by email. Anyone who does is not us. Report it to security@gabispay.com.

sections.heading: Reporting a vulnerability
sections.body: If you have found a security issue, write to security@gabispay.com with enough detail to reproduce it. We will acknowledge within two business days, keep you updated, and credit you if you would like us to. Please do not test against other people’s accounts.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
sections.body: Freeze your cards from the app immediately, then contact support. A frozen card cannot be charged, and freezing costs nothing if it turns out to be a false alarm.

pages.ctaBody: security@gabispay.com — acknowledged within two business days.

faqs.question: How do I open an account?
faqs.answer: Download the app or open your account on the web, give your details, and verify your identity. Most people are done in under ten minutes.

faqs.question: What do I need to verify my identity?
faqs.answer: A government-issued ID and a selfie. Business accounts also need proof the business exists — a registration document or equivalent.

faqs.question: How long do transfers take?
faqs.answer: Local Nigerian transfers are usually instant. ACH into your USD account settles in one to three business days; wires are typically same day.

faqs.question: Why was my card declined?
faqs.answer: The app shows the actual reason — balance, a limit you set, or a merchant category. If it says none of those, contact support and we will trace it.

faqs.question: How do I freeze a card?
faqs.answer: Open the card and tap freeze. It takes effect immediately and you can unfreeze it just as fast.

faqs.question: Can I use gabis outside Nigeria?
faqs.answer: Yes. The account is built for people who earn in one place and spend in another.

faqs.question: How do I get my money out?
faqs.answer: Withdraw to any bank account you control, in any currency you hold, from the app.

faqs.question: Something went wrong with a payment — what now?
faqs.answer: Contact support with the reference. Failed payments are returned to your balance automatically; we will tell you when and why.
